correctness.rationale: The three homogeneous differential quadratics are obtained by direct differentiation and have no common projective zero on the unramified open. Their span therefore has dimension at least two. The normal sequence makes N_f(-4) globally generated of rank two and degree two, so its only possible splits are (1,1) and (0,2). At twist -6, Serre duality identifies the transpose of the H^1 map with the span map of the three quadratics, giving h^0(N_f(-6)) = 3 - rank(M_f). In characteristic two the middle column is identically zero, hence rank is exactly two; the exhibited maps give t^2, s^2, t^2. Away from two, taking the pencil spanned by P,Q is a smooth PGL_2 frame torsor modulo scalars, and its Plücker coordinates become the Wronskian coordinates by scaling the middle coordinate by 2. The basepoint-free open maps onto the distinct-root open, as also follows from disc(W) = 4 Res(P,Q). The collinearity incidence of three points on a line is irreducible; its determinant image is smooth at rank two by a nonzero cofactor. Intersecting with the distinct-root, no-common-zero open removes the rank-one locus. Pullback by the product of the smooth torsors gives a smooth irreducible divisor; the equations have degree two in each quadratic-pair factor. The exhibited dependent and independent rows remain of rank two and three, respectively, in every characteristic other than two, and their pairs are basepoint free. The statements concern fixed-source morphisms and the normal bundle of the map, not embedded images.
